raw_response:
I'm 66 years old, and I've been farming these 12 mu in Quzhou for 45 years. I know this land better than I know my own hands. My household has seven people — my wife, my son and daughter-in-law, their two children, and my elderly mother. My son works in a factory over in Handan and only comes back for the busy harvest and planting seasons, so most days it's just me and my wife carrying the load. We watch every yuan because we don't have much cash to spare, and with my grandson starting middle school this year, the expenses are only going up.

This year I'm sticking with what I know: 8 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, and 4 mu in cotton. I thought about dropping the cotton because at my age the picking wears me out, but my daughter-in-law promised to help, and last year's cotton price was decent. The wheat-maize is our foundation — we eat some, sell some, and it's steadier than cotton. I don't gamble on new varieties or fancy methods. I do what worked last year, unless something forced me to change.

**Winter wheat (8 mu):** I'll plant around October 10th, same as every year. I'm using Jimai 22, an improved variety. The seed costs me about 45 yuan per mu — I buy fresh seed every two or three years to keep the vigor up. For fertilizer, the extension station recommends 20 kg of nitrogen per mu, but urea got expensive again and I'm not made of money. I'll put down a base before planting with compound fertilizer mixed with urea — that gives me about 12 kg nitrogen — and then in late March at jointing, I'll look at the wheat. If it's turning yellow, I'll topdress another 6 kg with urea. Total around 18 kg nitrogen per mu. I'll also add some phosphorus and potassium in the base, about 5 kg and 3 kg per mu respectively. I'll irrigate three times: once after planting to help the seeds settle, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading in April. Each irrigation runs me about 30 yuan per mu for the electricity to pump. The water table has dropped over the years, but my well still reaches. I'll spray herbicide once after planting to keep the weeds down. I hire a combine for harvest in early June — I'm 66, I can't swing a sickle like I used to — and I need two or three days of hired help to bag the grain and get the maize planted fast. I expect about 400 kg per mu if the spring weather cooperates.

**Summer maize (8 mu):** This goes in the ground right after wheat harvest, around June 12th to 15th. The window is tight — sometimes only five or six days — so I hire a planter to drill the seed. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, about 65 yuan per mu. At planting I band compound fertilizer in the row, giving me about 16 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. In mid-July at the big trumpet stage, if the rains haven't been good, I'll side-dress urea for another nitrogen boost. Maize needs less babysitting than wheat. I'll irrigate twice — at silking in late July and grain filling in August — unless we get lucky with summer thunderstorms. I spray herbicide and keep an eye out for corn borer; if I see damage, I'll spray insecticide. Harvest is late September into early October, and I hire a combine for that too. I figure 450 kg per mu is a reasonable expectation.

**Cotton (4 mu):** I plant around April 22nd. I use a hybrid cotton seed, about 55 yuan per mu. Cotton is tricky — too much nitrogen and you get tall vines with no bolls. I'll put down about 13 kg nitrogen per mu total, split three ways: base before planting, first topdress at squaring in June, and second at flowering in July. I also add 5 kg phosphorus and 4 kg potassium per mu in the base. I irrigate twice, at flowering and boll setting. The real headache is pests — bollworm is always lurking — so I spray insecticide two or three times and use herbicide for weeds. The picking starts in mid-September and goes through October, three or four rounds. That's the hardest part for me now. My daughter-in-law and wife do a lot of it, but I'll probably hire five days of village women to help pick, paying them by the jin. I'm hoping for 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

**Labor and costs:** The wheat-maize takes about 12 family labor days and 3 hired days. The cotton is a labor sponge — about 22 family days and 5 hired days. My son comes back for wheat harvest and maize planting, thank goodness. All told, my input costs will run about 4,800 yuan this year — seed, fertilizer, diesel for pumping, pesticides, and hired labor. That's a big chunk of cash for a small farm like mine. I could probably push the fertilizer higher and squeeze out more yield, but if I spend that money and then a drought hits or prices drop, my family feels it. I'd rather sleep soundly knowing I have a little cash in the cabinet for emergencies.
